Transport/Transit - In this mode, the MTV is in transit between deployment sites, homeport, or away port. No personnel are onboard in this mode, and the MTV is being towed or connected to a tow vessel. 3. In-service - In this mode, the MTV is actively being moored, un-moored, or in the service of testing a CEC. Personnel may be onboard for limited durations to assist automated systems with MTV functions, troubleshooting, or other testing-specific tasks. 4. De-Mobilization - In this mode, the MTV is preparing for standby mode after a CEC testing campaign or transport, including unloading user and MTV-specific equipment and supplies. This can be at the MTV’s homeport or a port near a deployment site. 5. Standby - In this mode, the MTV is at homeport or away port for personnel rest, weather/environmental, or user-requested reasons when reserved for a user. This also includes days where the MTV is mechanically and administratively prepared for at-sea operations but not reserved for a user. Personnel may be on board to inspect equipment or perform minor maintenance activities. 6. Maintenance - This mode includes planned minor maintenance, shipyard overhaul (homeport), or emergency repairs (homeport or away port). It includes days undergoing overhauls, dry-docking, or other scheduled or unscheduled repairs during which the MTV is Final Technical Report 49/57 unavailable for service. This mode also includes at-sea shakedown of overhauled equipment and certification activities where the MTV is unavailable for project activities. a. Minor Maintenance – Minor maintenance may be performed while the MTV is at port for fitting out, general upkeep, routine outfitting, and minor pier side maintenance. b. Major Maintenance/Haul-out – Major maintenance may or may not include haul- out or moving the MTV to a service location by water. c. Inspection/Certification – This refers to a day or more in which the ship is undergoing an inspection by USCG, ABS, or another regulatory or inspection body. 7. Outreach - In this mode, the MTV is primarily devoted to conducting an open house or other public outreach event. This may be at homeport or away port and involves personnel aboard to prepare for events, during, and clean up after events. 8. Out of Service - In this mode, the MTV is laid up out of service for an extended period for reasons of economy, unemployment, unfitness for service, or another externality. Personnel may be aboard periodically for inspection of the vessel or equipment. 14.2 User Classes The following types of MTV user classes are expected.
